note: A close and readable rendering of difficult kāvya verse; the closing line about the 'roaring masters' is uncertain but is flagged as such by the translator.

errors.english: that very same fire is not a cause of diminution for smoke and the like, but rather produces it
errors.why: The Tibetan only says fire is like that (not a cause of diminution) with respect to smoke; 'but rather produces it' is the translator's unmarked addition.

note: Sound rendering of the two kinds of destruction and the causes of diminution in the argument on contradiction.

errors.english: What is called "impossibility otherwise" the necessity that the effect cannot exist without the cause
errors.why: The verse just says 'that which is inexplicability otherwise'; the unmarked gloss is not in the Tibetan and wrongly narrows avinābhāva to a causal relation.

fix.find: What is called "impossibility otherwise" the necessity that the effect cannot exist without the cause

errors.english: The engagement does not occur because of certainty.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the three-mode reason does not operate to produce certainty (it is inconclusive), not that certainty prevents it from operating.

fix.find: The engagement does not occur because of certainty.
fix.replace: It does not serve to establish certainty.

errors.why: The verse says the reason (as invariable concomitance) never resides in the three modes; 'separately' is added and changes the claim.

errors.english: Is the sensation accompanied by the mosquito.
errors.why: The Tibetan says one knows for certain that this sensation was produced by something with a mosquito; the English splits the sentence and loses the agent of 'produced'.

errors.english: Even if the property of the subject (paksadharmatā) is a non-entity,
errors.why: dngos med here means the pakṣadharmatā is actually absent, not that it is a non-entity; the point is that the reason works without it.

note: Verse structure is kept, but several key lines of Pātrasvāmin's argument against the three-mode reason are misconstrued.

errors.english: refers to the two aspects of the object and the cognition related to the object. It is the conditioned entity itself, such as a flask, which is produced from a collection of causes and conditions and is capable of being established without depending on others.
errors.why: Substance is the conditioned entity able, without depending on anything else, to accomplish the two kinds of purpose related to the object and to cognition; 'the two' are the object of bsgrub nus pa, not what substance 'refers to'.

fix.find: refers to the two aspects of the object and the cognition related to the object. It is the conditioned entity itself, such as a flask, which is produced from a collection of causes and conditions and is capable of being established without depending on others.
fix.replace: is the conditioned entity itself, such as a flask, produced from a collection of causes and conditions, which is able, without depending on anything else, to accomplish the two kinds of purpose, those related to the object and those related to cognition.

errors.english: Those things established as the basis for the phenomena and subject are the second category.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the property and property-bearer that take those qualities as their basis are the second kind; the English inverts basis and what rests on it.

note: Generally readable account of observation and of the substance/quality division, but the definition of substance is misparsed.

errors.english: because what does not remain to destroy it itself remains
errors.why: The reason is that when the destroyer is not present the thing remains by itself, so a cause of its remaining is pointless; the English garbles this.

note: Faithful line-by-line commentary rendering with one garbled reason clause.
Accurate rendering of Candrakīrti on the king's sin and pride, including the butcher's-son anecdote and the root verses.

errors.english: You and the cowherd's mother will come to know through unrest
errors.why: ma zhi ba is the name Śāntā (the cowherd's mother, as the comment's 'thrown by Śāntā's hand' shows), not 'unrest'; the comment also marks the lemma as running up to the words about the curd pot.

fix.find: You and the cowherd's mother will come to know through unrest
fix.replace: You and the cowherd's mother, Śāntā, will come to know

errors.why: tshang here is 'nest', glossed on the next side as 'a dwelling', not 'complete'.

note: Usable word-gloss commentary, but a proper name is rendered as a description and some lemmas are misread.

errors.english: is intended to be the producer of its own form
errors.why: mngon par sems pa is 'falsely conceives/presumes' (abhimāna), as the next side's mngon par rlom pa confirms, not 'intends'; the following 'nothing other than what is intended' carries the same error.

errors.english: Mimamsaka [note: original: "skyes mos", referring to the Mimamsa school of Indian philosophy]
errors.why: skyes mos is not a Tibetan name for the Mīmāṃsakas (dpyod pa pa); the identification is a guess presented as fact.

note: The dream/waking validity argument is followed, but the final passage on the cognition of absence misreads the key verb.
Faithful rendering of the general and specific, figurative and literal characteristics of the four truths.
Accurate rendering of the Pañjikā on the mind of the three times and the plantain-tree simile.
